cause_assessments.reason: Original same-state frames [25, 26, 27] show the identical curved cuts at the two-line disclosure’s leading edge with its entire native activation box inside the viewport. The production Compose TextButton uses zero content padding and its default rounded shape; the component owns this disclosure and its typography. The clip moves with the control across scroll positions, so host viewport clipping, missing state evidence and resizing of contact sheets do not explain it. This is one disclosure-shape clipping cause manifested in both qualitative atoms, not two independent bugs.

Original fully visible disclosure text is cut by its own curved control boundary at multiple scroll offsets; the host viewport is clear of the affected letters. The production component uses a TextButton with zero content padding and full-width copy at enlarged P2 text. This supports component-owned text masking/occlusion, not a torn capture or scroll-edge artifact. The wrapping and overlap observations describe the same local defect, not independent bugs.

The component has lost b during revision replacement; the continued summary/callback failures are manifestations of that product state defect. Source, changed notice, actual fixture and stable native bindings establish that the caller update reached the live component. This assessment does not infer a handler from a label or a blocked disabled action. The successful native xcui_tap at stimulus action 8 emits bicycle:submit:a; the exact submitted-state frames retain that callback interval and fixture binding, confirming the wrong forwarded set after demonstrated activation.

Exact-state originals and native summary report only Brake inspection / 20 min after reselection of a; b remains visibly unselected despite fixture 1 specifying initial b. Successful reselection callback and stable current input/event bindings are present. This persists from the component replacement-selection defect and explains the missing Wheel alignment / 35 min contribution. It is not a text-wrapping defect or an old caller input.

clusters_one.reason: Both public themes use the same production SwiftUI submit label background plus PlainButtonStyle and native disabled modifier. Fully visible baseline originals show the same whole-control dimming and stable wrong solid fill while native enablement is correctly false. These are theme manifestations of one disabled rendering treatment. The exact platform compositing mechanism is inferred; direct mismatches and same implementation path establish membership.

Same-instance caller replacement delivers revision bicycle-1 with valid available initialSelectedIDs=[b]. Original/native states instead have no selected service; summary, primary enablement, and action fill all derive from that same selectedIDs state. Adding a later produces only a/20 min and submission emits only a. Both P1 and P2 use this same production component state path. The replaced color has a disabled-style contribution, but its required enabled role is already violated by the lost b state; it is assigned here once, with the indispensable upstream state defect. Exact SwiftUI closure/state mechanics remain unproved.

Across baseline, expanded and submitted P2 originals, the same Show/Hide native disclosure has matching curved cuts in leading glyphs away from host viewport edges. The production Compose TextButton uses zero content padding and full-width copy under the same rounded clipping treatment. Wrapping (lost glyphs) and overlap (local occlusion) are two manifestations of this one component source cause, repeated in three states.

clusters_two.reason: Both P1 light and P2 dark baseline actions correctly have no selected services and native enabled=false. Source explicitly fills the label with the approved disabled palette then applies PlainButtonStyle and .disabled. Original own/common PNGs and approved-strip samples show the same whole-button disabled rendering changes the final owned fill. The palettes differ but the same production style path and state trigger explain both rows. The exact platform compositing implementation remains inferred, without weakening the shared observed style cause.

The same component TextButton disclosure uses PaddingValues(0.dp), full-width copy and the default rounded button shape. Exact-state originals show identical curved removal of leading portions of both wrapped lines in P2 baseline, expanded and submitted, clear of the viewport edge. Wrapping (lost readable glyph portions) and overlap (local text occlusion) are separate questions about that one clipping defect. No separate independent bug is invented per state or aspect.

In both P1 and P2, the live fixture advances to revision bicycle-1 with initialSelectedIDs=[b], stable new input hash and successful caller_fixture_update. The component nevertheless has no selected b: summary is empty, primary action is disabled and its replacement fill is consequently wrong. Demonstrated subsequent a toggle adds a, then submitted summary and callback contain only a. The same lost incoming b explains these 12 downstream rows through the shared chosenServices reducer and callback forwarding in the original source. Replaced color is grouped with the missing incoming selection because its required enabled palette depends on that state; the separately observed baseline disabled-fill defect is a contributing rendering effect, not another independent replacement manifestation. Exact SwiftUI onChange/closure mechanism is not proven, but source ownership, stable delivered input and common native sequence establish this shared product-state cause.
